items.q: What happens to the total mass during a chemical reaction?
items.correct: It is conserved — atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed.
items.misconception: Mass can simply disappear, e.g. when a candle burns.
items.random_wrong: A reaction always increases the total mass.
items.why: In a closed system the same atoms are present before and after, so total mass is unchanged.

items.q: Is melting ice a chemical reaction?
items.correct: No — it is a physical change; the substance is still water.
items.misconception: Yes, melting is a chemical reaction.
items.random_wrong: Chemical reactions never make new substances.
items.why: Chemical reactions form new substances; melting only changes the state.

items.q: What happens to a catalyst in a reaction?
items.correct: It speeds up the reaction without being used up.
items.misconception: It is used up and must be replaced.
items.random_wrong: It increases the amount of product formed.
items.why: Catalysts lower the activation energy and are unchanged at the end; they don't change the final yield.
